story: Last night of the World's Hottest Tour. 80,000 people screaming every word in unison — you couldn't hear him over the crowd, and that was the point.
Renaissance opened and the whole stadium turned chrome. Felt like stepping into the future for two hours.
Rain the whole set. Nobody moved for shelter. 'Fake Plastic Trees' under a grey sky and 100,000 wet strangers crying together.
DAMN. just dropped. The desert dust lit up red under the stage lights when DNA hit. Pure adrenaline.
Lasers bouncing off 300-million-year-old rock walls during 'Let It Happen'. Felt like the mountains were breathing.
The pyramid set. The show that changed live electronic music forever. I was 16 in the crowd and nothing was the same after.
MOTOMAMI live. The motorcycle, the choreography, 65,000 people doing the moves. Spain met México and the roof came off.
Harbour behind the stage, '505' as the last song, the sails of the Opera House glowing. Unreal setting for a band.
The lifeguard-tower stage, the diving board. 'Snooze' and 20,000 phone flashlights. Soft and massive at the same time.
The LED wristbands turned the entire stadium into one breathing organism during 'Fix You'. Cried, not ashamed.
Sunset set. He sampled the crowd's screams live and looped them back. We literally became the song.
70,000 people raging in an actual ancient Roman stadium. Ancient ruins + UTOPIA. Most surreal rage of my life.
